title: Table 9.16 Pathological features of glandular lesions in the liver
tablehtml:
Entity

Characteristics

Gross

Histological

Immunohistochemical

Von Meyenburg complex (microhamartoma)

Typically microscopic lesions; rarely grossly identified as multiple minute nodules, related to portal tracts; usually < 5 mm

Irregular or rounded ductal structures lined by flattened or cuboidal epithelium; lumina may contain proteinaceous fluid or bile concretions; dense fibrous stroma; usually portal or periportal in distribution

Positive for CK7 and CK19

Bile duct adenoma

Whitish, firm, discrete nodule; usually < 20 mm

Small tubules lined by cuboidal epithelium, may contain mucin; inflamed or hyalinized fibrous stroma; often contains pre-existing portal tracts

Positive for CK7, CK19, and often foregut antigens (MUC6, MUC5AC, TFF2, D10, 1F6); CRP and albumin-ISH can be positive

Biliary adenofibroma

Circumscribed, solid-microcystic or macrocystic tumour; as large as 160 mm

Tubulocystic structures with hypocellular fibrotic stroma; single-layered cuboidal epithelium; cytoplasmic projection (apocrine snout-like); sometimes with intracystic papillary growth, mitotic activity, or cellular atypia

Positive for CK7, CK19, and occasionally CA19-9

Serous cystadenoma

Circumscribed, sponge-like tumour, with microcysts filled with clear watery fluid; any size

Multiple small cysts separated by thin fibrous septa, lined by a single layer of glycogen-rich clear cuboidal cells

Positive for CK7, CK19, MUC6, and α-inhibin

Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, small duct

Mass-forming (90%) or mixed mass-forming and periductal-infiltrating tumour (10%)

Haphazardly arranged, anastomosing tubules; solid nests; cuboidal or columnar cancer cells; rare intracytoplasmic or extracellular mucin; sclerotic fibrous stroma

Positive for CK7, CK19, CRP, albumin-ISH, N-cadherin, CD56 (50%), and p53 (30%)

Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, large duct

Periductal-infiltrating (15%), mass-forming (30%), combination of the two (50%), or intraductal growth (5%)

Gland-forming adenocarcinoma; small cancer cell nests in poorly differentiated cases; columnar cancer cells with cytoplasmic mucus; extracellular mucin; abundant desmoplastic stroma; highly infiltrative growth

Positive for CK7, CK19, S100P, MUC5AC (70%), and p53 (30%); loss of SMAD4 (30%)

Metastatic adenocarcinoma

Single or multiple firm nodules of any size; rarely intrabiliary extension (e.g. colorectal cancer)

Adenocarcinoma with variable appearance; often associated with necrosis and mitotic figures; irregular infiltration into the surrounding parenchyma or portal tracts

Variable phenotypes depending on primary sites; usually negative for CRP and albumin-ISH

CRP, C-reactive protein; ISH, in situ hybridization.
